fields.name: is_approximate
fields.documentation: DEPRECATED, retiring with the six session_/epoch_/event_ reference subclasses (#65 increment 3). CHANGE 2 of the signed walkthrough deletes it: approximateness belongs where there is a quantity to qualify (start / duration / clock_tolerance), and the field is empirically vacuous -- eleven writers, every one a hardcoded `true`, expressing 'we do not know exactly when', which having no start and no duration already says. THE ABSENCE IS THE IMPRECISION. Not removed yet ONLY because the strict-fields check would quarantine every live anchor whose emitter still writes it.

fields.name: clock_tolerance
fields.documentation: The stated precision of the TIMELINE these times are expressed on -- NOT of any one value. ABSENT = no stated tolerance. De-encoded from NDI's `approx_` clocktype prefix, which documents +/-5 s in a docstring (+ndi/+time/clocktype.m:21,23,26): approx_utc -> clock: utc + clock_tolerance {seconds: 5}. The migrator supplies the 5 from writer semantics -- transcription, not invention. On the ROOT because a tolerance-bearing UTC time can be an absolute_reference (a wall-clock instant) or a relative_reference (offsets on the UTC clock); for absolute_reference the timeline is UTC by construction.

fields.name: seconds
fields.documentation: Canonical time value -- the normalised, cross-document comparable number.

fields.name: source_unit
fields.documentation: The unit exactly as given by the source (lossless provenance).

fields.name: source_value
fields.documentation: The number as given by the source, in `source_unit`.

fields.name: approximate
fields.documentation: True when the value is approximate.
